data.title: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) & prevention of parent-to-child transmission (PPTCT)
data.summary: Antivirals & ART · Antiretroviral prophylaxis regimens (current NACO guidance)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Antiretroviral prophylaxis regimens (current NACO guidance)

## Mechanism of action
- ART given soon after exposure prevents establishment of infection in local dendritic cells and lymph nodes
- In pregnancy, maternal viral suppression plus infant prophylaxis prevents transmission

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Occupational PEP (needle-stick in dermatology procedures, splash on mucosa) and non-occupational PEP (sexual exposure, sexual assault)
- Risk assessment: exposure type (percutaneous, mucous membrane, broken skin) and source status
- PPTCT: all HIV-positive pregnant and breastfeeding women start lifelong ART irrespective of CD4 count

## Dose & formulations
- PEP: start as early as possible (ideally within 2 h, not beyond 72 h); preferred regimen TLD (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir) once daily for 28 days
- Baseline HIV test of exposed person; follow-up HIV tests at 6 weeks, 3 months (and 6 months as per programme)
- Immediate care: wash wound with soap and water, do not squeeze or use bleach; flush mucous membranes with water
- PPTCT: mother on TLD lifelong; infant prophylaxis with nevirapine syrup for 6 weeks (low risk), or zidovudine + nevirapine (dual prophylaxis) for 12 weeks if high risk (mother not virally suppressed/late diagnosis), with early infant diagnosis (DNA-PCR at 6 weeks)
- Hepatitis B: check vaccination status after needle-stick; give vaccine ± HBIG

## Adverse effects
- See component drugs; PEP side effects are usually mild with TLD

## Contraindications
- PEP not indicated if the exposed person is already HIV-positive or exposure is beyond 72 h

## Monitoring
- HIV test at baseline and follow-up; LFT/renal function if indicated; counsel safe sex/blood donation avoidance until follow-up negative

## Pregnancy & lactation
TLD is used in pregnancy for PEP and PPTCT.

## Viva points
- PEP within 72 h (ideally 2 h) for 28 days — TLD
- Infant prophylaxis: NVP 6 weeks or AZT+NVP 12 weeks (high risk)
- Lifelong ART for all pregnant women with HIV

## Note on sources
Khopkar's PEP and perinatal regimens (zidovudine-based, single-dose nevirapine) are outdated; only current NACO regimens are given here. Please confirm with the latest NACO technical guidelines.

_Sources: Current NACO PEP and PPTCT guidance; Khopkar ch.4 (Postexposure prophylaxis, perinatal transmission regimens — older regimens superseded). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
